about: How a line is sung on the live voice beyond what its body and its language say (native/vocaltract/soloist.mjs VoiceLine reads it; the owner, 14 November 2026: "we use JSON and other standard configuration file formats to store all physical constants, configurable variables, and similar objects").

flutter.about: The glottis's flutter over a sung phrase, in VocalTractLab 2.4's percent (vtl-stream `sing ... flutter=`; src/stream.rs LiveVoice::sing): Klatt's device against a held vowel's sameness in read speech (D. Klatt & L. Klatt 1990, "Analysis, synthesis, and perception of voice quality variations among female and male talkers", JASA 87(2), 820-857, doi:10.1121/1.398894) -- three sinusoids at 12.7, 7.1 and 4.7 Hz, each half a percent of F0 at the 25 percent 2.4's speakers' glottis shapes carry, 26 cents either way together, the same in every voice at every moment. `carried`: for a phrase that carries its singer's own pitch line (its transitions and vibrato, measured on sung F0: the line is its pitch whole); null leaves the speaker's own. 0 since 16 November 2026 (the owner, of a Kyrie sung with an ensemble's small vibrato: "There's aliasing, I think"; "on some of the lower notes more than the higher notes"): on a bass's held D3 the flutter's side tones stood 22 dB under its harmonics, and over them from 2 to 8 kHz, each upper partial a cluster of tones that are no harmonic's; without it 31 dB under, what is left its cycles' own jitter. What a singer's held note does of itself is in the line it carries since that evening: its wander, as Ternström and Friberg (1989) measured choir singers' straight tones, each singer's own (public/shared/vocal/sung-vibrato.json `wander`).

jitter.about: The folds' jitter on a sung line, in VocalTractLab 2.4's percent (the glottis's static `jitter`: random steps of the folds' phase, as strong at every rate up to the voice's own pitch; public/shared/vocal/sung-voice.js sets it as a singer's stream starts). 2.4's speakers carry 10 at every pitch, and its steps are a size in hertz: a soprano's share of her pitch, three times a bass's of his. Recorded singers' are a share of their pitch. Read one way throughout -- a held note's periods from its fundamental's zero crossings, each period's frequency held to the next, that contour's spectrum in cells of 0.6 Hz, as S. Ternström and A. Friberg (1989), "Analysis and simulation of small variations in the fundamental frequency of sustained vowels", STL-QPSR 30(3), 1-14, read eight choir singers (claude-scratch/gaps-voice/f0-spectrum.py, f0-spectrum-singers.py, 18 November 2026) -- VocalSet's eleven men's straight long tones (342 Hz at the median) fluctuate by 0.024 Hz a cell from 20 to 40 Hz (their middle half 0.018 to 0.039), its nine women's (532 Hz) by 0.030 (0.021 to 0.042), and Ternström and Friberg's bass (153 Hz) by no more than their analysis's floor, 0.01: 5.6 to 7.0 in a hundred thousand of the pitch. The engine with its turbulence noise on and no jitter: a tenor's 342 Hz 0.006, a soprano's 532 Hz 0.015, a bass's 147 Hz 0.002; with 10 percent 0.035, 0.038 and 0.030 -- the bass's three times what was measured, its steps spreading each upper partial of a low voice into a band of noise (the owner, 18 November 2026: "Hash noise is *digital*. It does not occur in human speech or song, and it sounds frequently, maybe even ubiquitously, in our model, so it must be traceable to something in our modeling or processing"). `percentPerHz`: the percent a hertz of a part's median pitch at which the engine, its noise on, stands at the recorded singers' median for that sex at the pitch they sang (6.7 percent at the men's 342 Hz, 7.3 at the women's 532); by it a bass at 147 Hz has 2.9 percent, within Ternström and Friberg's bound (3.3). One pitch a sex was measured, and a bound at a second: between and beyond them the share of pitch is held. What a held note does of itself more slowly is the wander its line carries (public/shared/vocal/sung-vibrato.json `wander`), the same study's.

stream.about: How native/vocaltract/sing-score.mjs sings a written part on the voice (read at its start; until 16 November 2026 written in its code). `settings`: vtl-stream's, but for the singer's body (its file and `anatomy=singer,...`) and `cores=` (the run's): VocalTractLab 2.4's speaker (version=2.4) on VocalWind's acoustics -- the passive core with its fitted wall-loss law, VocalWind 4.0's first step (acoustics=vocalwind; docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md, "Which engine is which") -- stepped as its physics asks and held there (oversampling=1, adapt=0), each step's system solved in 2.4's order (solver=envelope), its geometry made on one thread beside (workers=1), VocalTractLab's bugs mended (mended=1). `lookahead`: the frames the engine makes its geometry ahead of its acoustics, and `pull` the most samples a pull asks -- the Studio page's dial's own (native/vocaltract/live.mjs). `f0TauS`: the F0 time constant a phrase without a path of its own is sung with, VocalTractLab's measured 19.6 ms (docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md, "The F0 time constant"); a written part's notes carry their singer's path, sung at 0. `ringS`: how long a part's sound is let ring after its last phrase ends, s -- its last breath out and the tract's ring. `leadS`: how long before the piece's first beat every part's sound is kept, s -- the engine begins a phrase's onset the rules' reach (0.1 s) before its first note, so that a stem cut at the beat began in the middle of a sound that opens the piece on a vowel (the owner, 16 November 2026, of the selection's O magnum mysterium: "make sure there's no click at the start of a render"): every part the same, so they stay aligned, the piece's beats this much into its stems.

reArticulation.about: A repeated pitch within a melisma -- two notes at one pitch on one syllable -- sung as two notes: the lung pressure dipped into the second note's start, to `depth` of the syllable's over `rampS` and back over as long, as a singer marks each note of a melisma with the breath (the owner, 16 November 2026: "re-articulating repeated notes inside melismas (which would let us follow Palestrina's practice there)"; "you're also clear to pursue building these"). Designed, not measured: J. Sundberg 1992 (STL-QPSR 33(1) 49-64) sees such pulses in a coloratura passage only as 'faint reflections' of a warm-up's; a melisma's vowel is otherwise held over its notes (public/shared/vocal/plan-phones.js), so that two notes at one pitch would sound one. `rampParts`: a ramp is no longer than one part in this many of either note. `samePitch`: two notes are at one pitch where they differ by less than this, semitones. `joinedS`: the second follows the first where its start is within this of the first's end, s.

line.about: How native/vocaltract/soloist.mjs lays a sung line out for the engine (in its code until 17 November 2026; research/REGISTRY_PLAN.md, "The census"). `leastNoteS`: the least length a note is planned with, s. `phraseAfterReaches`: a silence of this many times the engine's rules' reach (its least pause before a phrase) ends a phrase and begins another, so that each phrase's score begins after the last has ended. `pauseLeastS`: a silence shorter than this between two phones of one phrase is not sung as a pause, s. `listed`: how many words a warning names before it says how many there are.

openToPitch.about: A woman's vowel opened toward the next more open one where her pitch passes its first resonance, as sopranos do (design H2: .claude/handoffs/trunk-vocalwind.md, "Later still: the squeak's design"; the owner, 16 November 2026: "Render now, then H2"). E. Joliveau, J. Smith & J. Wolfe 2004, "Vocal tract resonances in singing: the soprano voice", JASA 116(4), 2434-2439: sopranos keep speech's first resonance while their pitch is under it, and "once f0 exceeds this value of R1 ... R1 increased with f0 so that R1 was approximately equal to f0", from 600 to 1,000 Hz. Each body's first resonances asked of its own engine as its part begins (vtl-stream `resonance`: the passive core's network in frequency), at `steps` shares of the way between each two neighbours of a chain; a vowel sung where its note's pitch passes its own is opened by the least share whose resonance reaches the pitch, no further than the chain's last. Asked by native/vocaltract/sing-score.mjs --open-vowels, for the voice types `voiceTypes` (men's not until N. Henrich, J. Smith & J. Wolfe 2011 is read: research/SOURCES_TO_FETCH.md); `chains` each language's vowels from closest to most open, front and back, else `default`'s.

closeVowels.about: How native/vocaltract/close-vowels.mjs finds the share by which a singer opens a sung close vowel (the owner's yes of 17 November 2026 to its design: research/VOCALWIND_FITS.md, Next, 2, "Its first step"), and where its table is kept. `vowels`: the close vowels, each opened toward the next of its language's chain (`openToPitch.chains`). `bodies`: each sex's voice types whose bodies are read, each at the middle of its type -- its preset's speakers evenly weighed (voices/voice-types.json), its singer at `quantiles` of its tract's and its folds' spans. `steps`: the shares tried, from 0 to 1. `harmonics`: how many of a note's first harmonics are held to the recorded singers'. `nearDb`: how near two shares' distances from the recorded are for them to count as as near as each other, dB -- under what one body of a sex differs from another by on these notes (about 1 dB) -- the lesser share then kept, so that a gain too small to tell opens no vowel. `way`: which of the recorded singers' ways of singing a long tone is the target (voices/measured-long-tones.json `ways`): their straight tone, as the engine's held note has no vibrato. `mark` and `seconds`: the dynamic the vowel is sung at on the engine, at its held pressure, and how long it is held. `held`: the held note as it is sung and read, each in seconds: `lead` from the engine's clock to the phrase's start, `pause` the silence before and after the vowel, `rise` and `fall` the pressure's rise to the mark's and its fall after the vowel, `ring` the sound pulled after the phrase's end, `skip` and `short` the vowel's start and end left out of what is read (its onset and its release), `f0Every` the spacing of the pitch's points. `table`: the file in voices/ the shares are written to and the singer reads.

switches.about: What native/vocaltract/sing-score.mjs sings a part with where nothing else is asked (the owner, 17 November 2026: "wherever something performs better with a switch on, turn the switch on - ensure that our defaults are our best-performing approach"): each switch's `default`, and `better`, what was measured to sing better with it -- or `not`, why it is not the default yet and what would make it so. A switch is turned off for one run with --no-<switch>, a named one with `none`; with every one off the voice is VocalTractLab 2.4's on the passive core, as the parity tests hold it. Until that day each was off unless asked, and the selection the owner submitted on 16 November 2026 asked for four of them by hand (--tissue speaker --open-vowels --fold-law --level-held).

tissue.better: each body's walls its speakers', as measured of people like them (Fant 1972: a woman's lighter than a man's, their resonance 1.14 times), where 2.4 gives every speaker one wall: a measured part in a file's place; sung so in the selection the owner submitted (16 November 2026)

fossa.better: a man's piriform fossa laid where it is measured to have its trough, 4.65 kHz, where his file's 2.5 cm puts it at 5.2 (voices/speakers.json `fossa`, its sources there): a measured part in a file's place. It moves a body's first three resonances 4 Hz at most. Measured on the selection's tenor with the fold law, held [a] and [o] at mf on three pitches (17 November 2026): his band from 4 to 5 kHz a decibel deeper and from 5 to 8 kHz 1 to 3 dB stronger, each toward eleven recorded men's on their own vowels (voices/measured-long-tones.json: their deepest band from 4 to 5 kHz), no band more than 2 dB the other way

open-vowels.better: a woman's vowel opened toward the next more open one where her pitch passes its first resonance, as sopranos do (Joliveau, Smith & Wolfe 2004): on the Latin Kyrie's Cantus her [i] on D5 had its band from 2 to 4 kHz 12.3 dB over its fundamental, a squeak; opened, 12.4 under (docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md); sung so in the selection the owner submitted

close-vowels.better: a sung close vowel, [i] or [u], opened toward the next more open one of its language's chain by the share recorded singers' first harmonics ask (voices/close-vowels.json, each share sung on the engine as it plays: native/vocaltract/close-vowels.mjs): a man's Latin [u] 0.2 of the way to [ɔ] brings its first four harmonics from 12.1 dB to 3.7 dB of eleven recorded men's, his [i] 0.4 toward [ɛ] from 8.5 to 3.2; a woman's stay as her pitch already opens them. In its étude of "Tu es Petrus" the men's long [u] has its band from 1 to 2 kHz 8 to 13 dB fuller than the submission's and 2 to 4 kHz 7 to 12 dB, the bass's top unchanged. Heard by the owner, 17 November 2026: "the most recent render you showed me was the best so far, I think; with that said, I'll defer to the literature with regard to the physics and aim mostly to use my aesthetic judgement as a sanity check". What it does not mend: the band from 2 to 4 kHz and the cluster from 4 to 5 kHz, which are the larynx's and the source's (research/VOCALWIND_FITS.md, Next, 2).

fold-law.better: each body's folds by the fold fit's law (design C): the softest notes 22 to 26 dB over measured singers' where 2.4's own shape has them 30 to 33, a pitch's extent from them to ff 15 to 19 dB where it was 9 to 11 (voice-range.mjs --fold-law; docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md); sung so in the selection the owner submitted

level-held.better: each mark's level held as the line rises, a high note no louder than its mark sings at the middle of its range (the owner, 16 November 2026: "Aim to get our system to be able to sing high without forcing loud like that"; "Yes, level held"; voices/sung-levels.json); sung so in the selection the owner submitted

sung-folds.not: the singer's folds of 17 November 2026, in the fold law's place. As first fitted they are too dull: 22 to 28 dB under twenty recorded singers from 5 to 16 kHz, where the fold law is 7 to 16 under (docs/VOCAL_TRACT.md, "Against twenty recorded singers"): their fit held the upper band under one soprano's bounds and up to nothing. With their contact hard (--contact 0) they stand 6 to 10 dB nearer the singers' own "o" from 2 to 4 kHz than the fold law in the men and 5 in the woman, within 3 dB of it above 5 kHz in the men and 6 to 8 dB further in the woman (voices/measured-long-tones.json: twenty singers' long tones by vowel), with two more short low notes hardly pitched of 673 -- nearer for the men, further for the woman, and their held levels are not measured with that contact. The default once the fit held to the recorded singers on both sides has run (research/VOCALWIND_FITS.md, Next, 2) and measures nearer them than the fold law in every band

soft-least.not: the softest mark sung at the least pressure a trained singer sings at: measured, p 4.5 to 6.3 dB softer and mp 2.5 to 2.9 against mf, every note sounded, pp to ff then 19 to 30 dB. Twenty recorded singers' forte stands 7 to 13 dB over their own pp on one long tone (voices/measured-long-tones.json), which the fold law's marks, some 9 dB apart, already span: what this adds is a voice's whole extent, more than a mark's. And its table is the sung folds' (voices/sung-levels-sung-folds-soft-least.json): it is sung only with them. Not the default unless marked dynamics measured in singers ask for it

contact.not: the sung folds' contact softness asked for by hand, in their law's place (cm): a trial's switch

ventricle.not: a laryngeal ventricle of a given volume (cm3): fitted against the recorded singers' envelope it gains under 2 dB in any speaker and none in one, its size not settled (native/vocaltract/ventricle-fit.mjs, run 202611170836)
